correctness.rationale: For each coordinate the two state matrices use the Bernoulli indicator of that coordinate only; independence across coordinates is unnecessary for the expected squared norm. On symmetric matrices the resulting covariance map has the displayed three-dimensional matrix Q and preserves the PSD cone, so its spectral radius is a nonnegative real eigenvalue. At M=0 it is strictly below one. Direct expansion of det(I-Q) gives p(1-beta)F, and the quadratic has one positive zero. Continuity plus the absence of eigenvalue 1 gives subcritical stability; at the root the radius is one by continuity and singularity of I-Q. Above the root det(I-Q)<0, so the real monic characteristic polynomial has a zero >1, completing the sign argument implicit in the frozen proof. For a nonzero initial coordinate and zero velocity the time-one second-moment matrix is positive definite and dominates a positive multiple of a PSD Perron eigenmatrix. This eigenmatrix has positive error diagonal for M>0, which proves a positive lower bound at equality and exponential growth above it in that coordinate. Differentiation in p yields the weakest-row criterion, and substituting p=0 and M=1 respectively verifies the limiting root and the strict smoothing threshold. The signed-mean 2x2 Jury test is independent of this classification. Nondecay refers to not tending to zero, not monotonicity or a pathwise assertion. The frozen symbolic/path checks were read, not run, and are not needed for the all-parameter proof.
